target_customer: Developers and teams building computer-use agents, plus individuals who want agents to run on cloud or local desktops
problem: Computer-use agents need safe, isolated desktops to click and type in, and running them on a developer's own machine is risky and hard to scale.
business_model: Open source core (MIT) with paid cloud sandboxes and subscription tiers for Cua Spaces
product_category: Developer infrastructure, sandboxes for computer-use agents

founders.name: Francesco Bonacci
founders.background_notes: YC page lists one founder. A Launch HN summary says he left Microsoft in early 2025 and started with Lume, a CLI for macOS VMs on Apple Silicon.

competitors.name: E2B computer use
competitors.what: Cloud sandboxes with desktop for AI agents

technical_complexity.rationale: Running macOS and Linux virtual machines with low overhead on Apple Silicon and streaming desktops to agents is solid systems engineering, though not research grade.

defensibility.rationale: The core is MIT licensed open source and anyone can fork it; adoption by other agent projects and community mindshare are the main assets.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Labs shipped their own computer-use tools and hosted environments in 2025; no acquisition of Cua found.

market_need_then: Anthropic released computer use in late 2024 and OpenAI Operator followed in January 2025, creating demand for safe sandboxes for agents.

branding.domain_note: Started as trycua.com and later moved to cua.ai.

identity.visual_style: Developer oriented site with a linked branding page
identity.voice_and_tone: Developer first, open source, footer reads made with keys in San Francisco

branding.community_and_virality: GitHub repo with roughly 15 to 17 thousand stars per directory listings, a Discord, and a Launch HN post on 2025-04-23.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong open source awareness among agent developers shown by GitHub stars and projects using it, but the name is hard to pronounce and no brand coverage was found.

outcome_analysis: Cua is active and early. A solo former Microsoft engineer built the Lume macOS VM tool, joined YC in Spring 2025 and gained developer attention through open source and a Launch HN, then added cloud sandboxes and paid Spaces tiers. Funding is not confirmed by a primary source and labs keep expanding computer-use offerings, so outcome is open.
notes: Aggregators (VC Backed, Nordic9, StartupHub) report a 500K pre-seed in June 2025 from 468 Capital, Orange Collective and Script Capital, while Caplight lists 1M total. No press release or primary source was found, so none is recorded as a round. Name origin not found.
